Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

range noun

how far something can reach

also within range, out of range, range of a weapon, within sight, out of sight

classical

Verg. A. 11.608: intrā jactum tēlī
Liv. 8.7.1: vix tēlī jactū ab statiōne proximā abesset

jactus, jactūs m.

noun, fourth declension

a throw; the range of a throw

Within range is intrā tēlī jactum; a spear’s throw away, tēlī jactū.

Other words

  • conjectus, conjectūs m. — a throw; range

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Liv. 28.14.19: nōndum ad tēlī conjectum vēnissent; Petr. 90.2: extrā tēlī conjectum (Lewis & Short)

    ad tēlī conjectum venīre, to come within range.

  • cōnspectus, cōnspectūs m. — sight, the range of the eyes

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Phaedr. App. 28.10: sēque ē cōnspectū abstulit

    in cōnspectū, within sight; ē cōnspectū, out of sight.

Examples

  • jamque intrā jactum tēlī prōgressus uterque substiterat

    and now each side had come within range and haltedVerg. A. 11.608–609

  • ita ut vix tēlī jactū ab statiōne proximā abesset

    so that he was hardly a spear’s throw from the nearest outpostLiv. 8.7.1

  • vēnātor citus nōn intellēxit sēque ē cōnspectū abstulit

    the hunter, in a hurry, did not understand, and went off out of sightPhaedr. App. 28.10

See also range, far.

SourcesLewis & Short: jactus · Lewis & Short: conjectus · Lewis & Short: conspectus
